sections.h2: How do I reach the Hardin County Recorder in Kenton?
sections.html:
The Hardin County Recorder is at One Courthouse Square, Suite 220, Kenton, Ohio 43326. Call 419-674-2252 or 419-674-2250, or fax 419-675-2802. Counter hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

The Auditor is in the same courthouse, Suite 250, at 419-674-2239, and keeps hours of 8:00 to 4:00 on weekdays. Since a conveyance has to touch both offices, a short walk down the hall is often how a deed gets done.

The Recorder's page links to an online search run through Kofile, and it points visitors to the Ohio Recorders' Association site for more fee information.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Hardin County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Hardin County is in west central Ohio, with Kenton as the county seat and largest city. It was created in 1820, organized in 1833, and named for John Hardin, a Revolutionary War officer. It has 470 square miles of land and borders Hancock, Wyandot, Marion, Union, Logan, Auglaize and Allen counties.

It is a small, mostly rural county. The 2020 census put 56.4% of residents in rural areas, and the population has been drifting down, from 32,058 in 2010 to 30,696 in 2020 and an estimated 30,072 in July 2025.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 74.7% (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $151,200.
  • Median gross rent: $793, and 12,944 housing units.
  • Median household income: $62,484, and mean commute of 23.6 minutes.
  • Building permits in 2025: 24.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts for Hardin County and Wikipedia for geography and founding.

sections.h2: Why does Hardin County insist on the Auditor's stamp?
sections.html:
The Recorder will accept a conveyance by mail only if the Auditor's stamp is already on the document. The office states it will not walk a conveyance through the map department and the Auditor's office for you.

Practically, that makes the order simple: map department and Auditor first, Recorder last. A seller who mails a deed straight to the Recorder should expect it to come back unrecorded. If you are selling from out of town, give your closing attorney or title agent the job of carrying the deed through those stops.

The Auditor's forms page offers the DTE 100 value statement, the DTE 100EX exemption statement and the DTE 101 homestead conveyance statement. It tells users to check with the Ohio Department of Taxation for the latest version before filling one in.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Hardin County?
sections.html:
Ohio sets the recording fee by statute, and the Hardin County Recorder's page sends readers to the state recorders' association for rates. Under ORC 317.32, a base fee of $17 plus a housing trust fund fee of $17 covers the first two pages, and $4 plus $4 covers each page after that.

The statute also lets a county charge a document preservation surcharge of up to $5. The Recorders' Association table, revised October 24, 2024, lists $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each additional page, and notes a surcharge not exceeding $5.00 per document may be added. Call the Hardin County Recorder to learn exactly what the county charges today.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require before a deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
The grantor must sign the deed and acknowledge it before an authorized official. ORC 5301.01 lists a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor as the persons who may take the acknowledgment and certify it.

Most sellers use a notary at the title company or a bank. The deed then goes to the Auditor with a completed DTE 100 value statement, or a DTE 100EX if the transfer is exempt. Ask the Hardin County Auditor for the conveyance fee rate and the transfer fee per parcel, because rates vary by county.

The format rules in ORC 317.114 apply here as everywhere in Ohio: readable print, black or blue ink, no highlighting, and blank margins at the top of the page for the stamps of the Engineer, Auditor and Recorder.

sections.h2: What does the Hardin County Auditor handle for a manufactured home sale?
sections.html:
A manufactured or mobile home taxed like real property has its own paperwork. The Auditor's forms page lists a County Manufactured and Mobile Home Registration Certificate (DTE 41), a Manufactured and Mobile Home Conveyance Fee Statement of Value and Receipt (DTE 100M) and a Statement of Reason for Exemption from the Manufactured and Mobile Home Conveyance Fee (DTE 100MEX).

The Auditor also lists the Application for Tax Refund or Waiver for Destroyed or Damaged Manufactured Homes (DTE 49). If the home sits on land you own, ask the Auditor whether the sale uses the real property forms, the manufactured home forms, or both.

The Auditor's Real Estate section also carries the 2 1/2% reduction application for a home (DTE 105C), the complaint against the valuation of real property (DTE 1) and the application for a deduction for destroyed or damaged property (DTE 26). A buyer who will live in the house should ask about the 2 1/2% reduction at closing.

sections.h2: How do Hardin County tax dates affect a sale?
sections.html:
The Hardin County Auditor serves as the county's chief assessor, and its page says a full reappraisal of real property takes place every six years with an update every three years. A seller should know where the parcel stands in that cycle, because a new value can change the tax bills a buyer inherits.

The Auditor's due-date list shows real estate tax bills for the first half of the year due February 11 and the second half due July 8, and it places the window for filing a valuation complaint with the Board of Revision between January 3 and March 31. Homestead and 2 1/2% rollback applications are listed as due on the first Monday of June. Check your current tax bill for exact dates, since weekends and holidays can move them.

  • Ask the title company how taxes will be split at closing.
  • Ask the Auditor if the parcel has a homestead reduction, since DTE 101 must go with the deed.
  • Keep a copy of the Auditor's stamped deed.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed straight to the Hardin County Recorder?
faqs.a: Only if the Auditor's stamp is already on it. Without that stamp the Recorder's Office will not take the conveyance, and it does not walk deeds through the map department or Auditor.

faqs.q: What hours does the Hardin County Recorder keep?
faqs.a: The office lists Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., at One Courthouse Square, Suite 220 in Kenton.

faqs.q: Who can notarize a deed in Ohio?
faqs.a: Under ORC 5301.01 a notary public, a county auditor, a county engineer, a mayor, or a judge or clerk of a court of record can take the acknowledgment. Most sellers use a notary.

faqs.q: Is there a Hardin County online records search?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder's page links to an online service and search provided through Kofile.

faqs.q: What if I do not know the Hardin County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Call the Hardin County Auditor at 419-674-2239. The Auditor collects the conveyance and transfer fees before the deed goes on to the Recorder.
